questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride. The horn button is usually located near the left handgrip.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for other vehicles around you before moving lanes.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because they make eye contact with you. Many drivers look directly at motorcyclists but still do not notice them.

questions.question: When following another vehicle as a beginning rider, you should:

options.text: Maintain a minimum four-second following distance.
Get as close to the other vehicle as possible.
Never be concerned about your following distance.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane so the driver can easily see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a minimum four-second following distance.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds of distance between themselves and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycle operators and other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Most conflicts between motorcyclists and other drivers happen at intersections. Be extra careful when entering and crossing intersections.

questions.question: When being passed, all of the following are potential hazards, except:

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors hitting you. Also be aware of wind gusts from the passing vehicle and objects thrown by passengers who are not paying attention.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
Is designed to take corners at any speed.
Should not be used for loading items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels, a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean at the same angle together. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to occur among:

options.text: Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often with untrained, beginning riders who do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean when you lean. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce crash risk?

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible and use clear signals. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Watch ahead for hazards and be ready to react. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: You should choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your space cushion and makes you visible.
Increases your space cushion and makes you visible.
Increases hazard risk and allows others to pass you.
Reduces hazard risk and lets you follow vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your space cushion and makes you visible.
questions.explanation: A good lane position gives you more space around you and makes other drivers aware of you. It helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, blind spots, and road hazards. It also keeps other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Moves to different positions in the lane as conditions change.
Stays in the same lane position at all times.
Weaves back and forth in the lane to be seen.
Rides only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moves to different positions in the lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists have three lane position choices. You should pick the safest position based on the road and traffic conditions around you.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: A left arm extended straight out means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left. You can use hand signals instead of or together with your turn signals.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it makes things worse. Instead, hold the handlebars tight without fighting the wobble. Slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you safely can.

questions.question: To see better before passing a vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left part of your lane.
Ride in the right part of your lane.
Ride in the middle of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane before passing. This improves your view ahead and makes oncoming traffic see you better.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is most likely a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular, white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Riding side-by-side with another rider:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it cuts off your escape routes.
Makes it easier to talk to each other.
Makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it cuts off your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside another motorcyclist. It limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated by your left foot. Lift the lever with your foot to shift up. Press it down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: Many things affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does NOT affect it?

options.text: How much alcohol a person drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: Several factors affect a person's BAC. These include how much alcohol they drink, how fast they drink it, and their body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see the wearer.
Do not help improve a rider's visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it easier for others to see the wearer.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrower view of the road so you can focus better.
You will have more time to react if other vehicles move.
You can more easily follow the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react if other vehicles move.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: For normal braking:

options.text: Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Always use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: After you enter a turn, roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
Do not worry about your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through the turn to stabilize your suspension. Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly through the turn.
